bed._what: Two spans in order, so the song starts on the drum smash, loops back to its own top, and never plays the breakdown. Owner: 'we want the song on loop basically but starting at the drum smash', and 'cut out the weird drum section with the moaning'.

segments._what: A -- the drum smash to the last full bar. 193.420 is the MEASURED re-entry after the breakdown, +12.98 dB, the largest onset in the song. The out point was 240.780; the owner cut it: ':46 - cut all of this part and go right to the drums so the entire song sounds like a loop'. The song's ENDING starts at 240.08 -- the level falls -11 -> -17 dB and keeps falling to digital silence at 241.95 -- and an ending is exactly what a loop must not contain. :46 on the credits clock is source 239.420; the cut is at 239.653152, the nearest beat in the bed's own tracked grid, 0.23 s later and still 0.43 s clear of the decay.

B -- the top of the song to the start of the breakdown, which is the part the loop exists to let people hear. 181.320 is where the level falls to about -13 dB and stays; ending here removes the 12.10 s 'moaning' section. The bed record's own committed excision found the same span independently (removed_sec 12.097596).

reveal._what: THE REAL REVEAL, and the owner named its time: ':22 is when I want the comic book shot, put the cast after'. 22.080 rather than a flat 22.000 because a measured +5.01 dB onset sits there -- 0.080 s, under three frames, so the cut lands on a hit instead of mid-bar. The earlier anchor (the song's opening crescendo, 9.080 s into span B) is kept below: it is why the loop exists, and it is what to fall back to if `at_sec` is ever removed.

cast_photos._what:
Owner: 'For the principal actors - remove the pfp icon and instead use a good shot of them from the CNCF contributor summit flickr feed.' The mechanism is built (tools/credits.summit_portrait): a person maps to {'file': <photo>, 'box': [x, y, w, h]} and the placard uses that crop instead of the PFP or the authored card.

IT IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. stories/summit-photos.json is twelve frames of ONE Maintainer Summit GROUP photograph -- there is no per-person shot in the feed. Picking a face out of a crowd and saying whose it is is a visual judgement AND a claim about a real person, the two things AGENTS.md says an agent may never make. automatable: no. Each box is the owner's to draw; until then every placard degrades to the verified avatar or the authored Guardian card.
